provenance.notes: This document prints no RELIC marker at all, only INSERT, AUTOGRAPH RELIC and AUTOGRAPH, so five relic programmes fell through to the default kind and were filed as relics from the Series 2 document instead: Major League Material Cards, 1989 Topps Baseball Relics, City Connect Swatch Collection, In The Name Relics and Cut Signatures. It also misspells its own header as "Topps Reverence Autogaph Patch Cards", corrected to match Series 2. Card #219 is interleaved in the PDF text and repaired deterministically to Christian Encarnacion-Strand, Cincinnati Reds, Rookie. One non-card section skipped: Social Media Follow Back Redemption Cards.

Cards #413, #424 and #481 print a league where the team would go — American League, Major League Baseball, National League — which is why those values are in teams.json. American League was added for this set; no card in the 2025 or 2026 checklists prints it. One non-card section skipped: Social Media Follow Back Redemption.

provenance.covers: the Traded Gimmicks variation; the Kevin Hart Gimmicks variation; the Kayfabe Rookies variation; the two factory set checklists
provenance.notes: Neither Topps checklist lists these two cards, in any section: #50 appears only as Juan Soto of the San Diego Padres. Both are variations of base cards — #50 shows Soto after his trade to the Yankees, and #250 shows Shohei Ohtani where the base card is Mookie Betts, a different player on the same number. Team abbreviations NYY and LAD are expanded to the forms Topps prints elsewhere in this set. Kevin Hart Gimmicks is eighteen cards with the comedian photoshopped into the foreground, every one a Phillie, and all eighteen verify against base.csv on number, name and team. Two claims about them are not recorded. That source says they are exclusive to Series One packs, but twelve of the eighteen carry Series 2 numbers and this set's Series 1 is #1-350 exactly, so the claim cannot be right as stated. And each is serial numbered to 52 — a joke about Hart's height — which has nowhere to go, because print_run belongs to a parallel and this is a variation checklist. Kayfabe Rookies is #697-700 with Jackson Holliday, Jackson Chourio, Jackson Merrill and Wyatt Langford where the base cards are Jordan Diaz, Gio Urshela, Sean Bouchard and Jose Altuve — four different players on four existing numbers, the same shape as 2026's Short Print Rookies. Topps prints no name for them and no checklist lists them, so the name is the one that source gives its section; teams and the RC designation are taken from where this set prints those players elsewhere. Trading Card Database describes the same four as the base factory set versions of those numbers, which is consistent and is why the 582 Montgomery Club entry says they are on the base checklist. Factory Set Rookie Variations is five cards in the retail factory set: #60, #141 and #553 keep their base players, while #697 and #698 carry Jackson Holliday and Jackson Chourio over Jordan Diaz and Gio Urshela. Trading Card Database lists factory set variations at #697-700 instead, adding Merrill and Langford and dropping the three lower numbers, so the two sources disagree on the extent; the five named here are what this source states. Factory Set All-Stars is five inserts in the All-Star Game factory set, numbered 1-5 of their own — base #1-5 are Ronald Acuña Jr., the Padres team card, Endy Rodríguez, Logan Webb and Owen White — so it declares no varies. Factory Set Kayfabe Rookie Bonus is the same four players as Kayfabe Rookies, #697-700, in the factory set rather than Series 2 packs, with different photography and COMPLETE SETS on the reverse. UNRESOLVED: #697 and #698 now sit in two factory set checklists at once, this one and Factory Set Rookie Variations, because that source describes both without saying whether they are the same cards. Trading Card Database calls its equivalent a five-card cello pack, which matches the Rookie Variations count, while also listing factory set variations at #697-700, which matches this one. Both are recorded as stated and one of them may be double-counting Holliday and Chourio.

provenance.source: Baseball Card Pedia, 2024 Topps — base parallels
provenance.covers: which parallels cover every base card
provenance.notes: "All 700 base cards are available in the following parallels", followed by 27 entries, recorded here as coverage: full. Printing Plates is one entry there, "set of four for each card", and is declared as four — Black, Cyan, Magenta, Yellow — because a plate is a distinct one-of-one a collector owns and one entry cannot record owning the cyan one. Serial numbers are that page's. Trading Card Database agrees on every figure it gives, differing only in calling the foilboards crackle foils and holofoils. Parallels it lists that are absent from the 700 sentence were not declared from this source; 582 Montgomery Club, All-Star Game and the Holiday family have since been declared from their own sections of the same site, and First Card, Golden Mirror and True Photo are still undeclared for want of a coverage statement. Golden Mirror Image is already a 700-row variation checklist in this set, and Team Color Border a partial parallel of 625.

provenance.source: Baseball Card Pedia, 2024 Topps — Holiday Parallels, All-Star Game Factory Set, 582 Montgomery Club
provenance.covers: the thirteen Holiday parallels, the All-Star Game and 582 Montgomery Club factory set parallels
provenance.notes: Three sections of that page, each naming a parallel the base-parallel sentence omits. The Holiday parallels come in two waves of seven and six. Series 1: Holiday, Egg and Rabbit unnumbered, Flowers /50, Umbrella /10, Watering Can /5, Birds one-of-one. Series 2: Hot Dog and Statue of Liberty unnumbered, Beach Umbrella /50, Sun /10, Fireworks /5, Waves one-of-one. Plain Holiday heads both lists, so it is declared over the whole set rather than scoped to a wave, which is what Trading Card Database says too — floral pattern in Series 1, dotted circles in Series 2. The other twelve are scoped. Each wave runs the same ladder, unnumbered / unnumbered / 50 / 10 / 5 / 1, so a theme's print run is never evidence of which wave it belongs to. Trading Card Database gives thirteen Holiday entries that pair one-for-one with these thirteen and agrees on every print run, but calls the Series 1 one-of-one Chicks where this page calls it Birds. They are one card: that PDF has no Birds anywhere, and the pairing is exact only when Birds is read as Chicks. The baseballcardpedia name is kept, which is this repo's tie-break wherever two sources name one parallel differently — that page is the one a reader can open and check. The sources do disagree on distribution: this page calls the Holiday parallels Blaster box exclusives, while Trading Card Database puts the Series 1 themes in Value Boxes and only the Series 2 themes in Blasters, and no distribution is recorded on them for that reason. All-Star Game is all 700 base cards on foilboard with an ASG 2024 logo in specially-marked All-Star Game factory sets; 582 Montgomery Club is a factory set sent to every club member at the end of 2024, each card on foilboard with the club logo. Both are declared as full coverage of Base, and both carry a caveat the schema cannot express: Trading Card Database records a 2024 factory set as numbering 697-700 Jackson Holliday, Jackson Chourio, Jackson Merrill and Wyatt Langford — the rookies held here in variations/factory-set-kayfabe-rookie-bonus.csv — where base.csv has Jordan Diaz, Gio Urshela, Sean Bouchard and Jose Altuve. A factory-set parallel therefore covers 696 base cards plus four variations, so full coverage of Base is right about 696 numbers and wrong about four. Declaring them that way was preferred to 700 rows copied out to correct four of them, or to coverage unknown on parallels whose extent is documented.

provenance.source: Baseball Card Pedia, 2024 Topps — 1989 Topps Baseball
provenance.covers: the Foil parallels of the 1989 Topps Baseball and 1989 Topps All Star Baseball inserts, and the All Star parallels
provenance.notes: Every 1989 Topps Baseball card also comes in Foil, and Foil in six colours: Green /99, Purple /75, Gold /50, Orange /25, Red /5 and Black one-of-one. Trading Card Database gives the identical six figures under its own name for the insert, 1989 Topps Baseball 35th Anniversary, listing each colour twice because it splits the insert by series. Declaring this removed two checklists rather than adding any. Topps' own documents carried the Foil parallel as two insert sections, 1989 Topps Baseball Foil Mega Box Cards in Series 1 and 1989 Topps Baseball Foilboard Mega Box Cards in Series 2, and both were byte-identical to blocks of the insert they parallel: the 100 rows numbered 89B-1 to 89B-100 and the 50 rows numbered 89B2-1 to 89B2-50. They were 150 rows that said nothing base 1989 Topps Baseball did not already say, and the wave each card belongs to stays readable from the 89B and 89B2 prefixes, so nothing was lost with them. The sources disagree on where Foil was sold. This page calls it exclusive to Monster and Giant Boxes; Trading Card Database says Mega box, and Topps titles both its sections Mega Box Cards. Mega Box Exclusive is recorded, on the manufacturer's wording backed by TCDB, and the distinction is real in this set — Topps Mega Stars is separately recorded as Giant/Monster Box Exclusive. Topps also names the two halves differently, Foil in Series 1 and Foilboard in Series 2, where both other sources describe a single Foil parallel; the single parallel is what is declared, and the six colour runs all carry Foilboard in their own names on every source. Both insert checklists were verified row by row against that page, 150 and 50, matching on every number and name but one: 89B-68 is Vladimir Guerrero there and Vladimir Guerrero, Sr. on that page, which reads as a disambiguation from 89B-32 Vladimir Guerrero, Jr. rather than a printed form, so Topps' wording is kept. The All Star insert had the same duplication, its Topps section 1989 Topps All Stars Baseball Foilboard Mega Box Cards being identical row for row to 1989 Topps All Star Baseball, and it is now a parallel too; that is what shows the Foil covers all 50. Its parallels come from Trading Card Database, since that page documents no parallel of the All Star insert at all, and its six Foil colours run the same ladder as the main insert: Green /99, Purple /75, Gold /50, Orange /25, Red /5, Black one-of-one. They are recorded as coverage unknown, along with the five parallels of the All Star insert itself — Black and Blue unnumbered, Gold /50, Platinum one-of-one, Red /10 — because naming a parallel and giving its print run is not saying how many cards it covers. The main insert's six are full only because that page states it. Trading Card Database calls the All Star Foil a Giant/Monster Box exclusive, not a Mega Box one, so the two Foils are recorded with different distributions. Both are named for the checklist they parallel rather than being called Foil, because a parallel that other parallels point at has to be named uniquely within the set.

provenance.source: 2024 Topps Baseball — Inserts and Related Sets, Trading Card Database
provenance.covers: the parallels of the 2023 All Topps Team, 2023 Greatest Hits Grand Gamers and Superstar Blueprint inserts
provenance.notes: Five parallels: Black /299, Blue unnumbered, Gold /75, Platinum one-of-one and Red /10, all recorded as coverage unknown because that database names them and prints their runs without saying how many of the twelve cards each covers. Baseball Card Pedia documents no parallel of this insert, so nothing corroborates a count. The same insert one year later, 2024 All Topps Team in 2025 Topps, does have all eight of its parallels declared as full coverage — from a statement on that site, not from the shape of the ladder, and the difference between the two years is what evidence exists rather than what the cards are likely to be. A sixth entry there, 2023 All Topps Team Autographs, is not recorded as a parallel: it is already an autograph checklist in this set, and its run is given as 25 or less, a range rather than anything printed on a card. The twelve rows of the insert were verified against Baseball Card Pedia and match on every number and name. 2023 Greatest Hits carries the same five parallels on the same runs — Black /299, Blue unnumbered, Gold /75, Platinum one-of-one, Red /10 — recorded as unknown for the same reason, and its autographs are likewise already a checklist here rather than a parallel. That two unrelated inserts share a ladder to the copy is worth stating: it is a house structure Topps applied across the product, not a fact discovered about either insert, and it is not evidence of coverage for either. That database adds that both were issued in Series One packs, which is recorded on neither, being a statement about the inserts rather than about their parallels. The thirty-one rows of Greatest Hits were verified and match on every number and name, including the three consecutive Shohei Ohtani cards at 23GH-12, 13 and 14 and the repeated players at 5 and 8, 9 and 20, 10 and 19, 2 and 27, 16 and 28. Grand Gamers is the third insert on that identical ladder, Black /299, Blue unnumbered, Gold /75, Platinum one-of-one, Red /10, unknown for the same reason, with its autographs again already a checklist. Three inserts now share it exactly, which makes it the default treatment for this product rather than a property of any one insert. A fourth insert found on the same five names and runs should be read as confirming that pattern, and still not as evidence of how many cards any of them covers — the ladder describes what colours exist, and coverage is the separate question of how much of a checklist each colour reaches. Its twenty-six rows verified and match on every number and name. Correction, and the reason the field is asserted rather than derived: the five All Topps Team parallels are full coverage, all twelve cards in each, asserted by this repo's owner. What that database gave was never going to settle it — coverage is a human judgement in this format precisely because sources name parallels far more often than they count them. Greatest Hits and Grand Gamers stand at unknown pending the same judgement, not because their evidence differs; it is identical. Superstar Blueprint is the fourth on the ladder, same five names and runs, and its autograph is already a checklist here — that database calls it Superstar Blueprint Autograph and numbers it by player initials, which is an autograph checklist and not a partial parallel for the reasons ROW-FORMAT now gives. It is recorded unknown, joining Greatest Hits and Grand Gamers, while All Topps Team is full. The three are not weaker evidence than the one; they are the same evidence awaiting the same person's judgement, and recording them as unknown in the meantime is the point of having the value. Its twenty-five rows verified and match on every number and name.

notes: One set issued in two waves. Team Color Border is a partial parallel, not a variation: it re-versions 625 of the 700 base cards, 300 in Series 1 and 325 in Series 2, and Topps prints it as a variation the way it does True Photo and the others corrected in 2026. Golden Mirror Image stays a variation, covering all 700, because it changes the photograph. Four sections Topps labels an autograph variation number their own cards and share no card number with any checklist, so they are declared as the autograph lists they are. Homerun Challenge Code Card stays per series: the two reuse codes on different cards.
